id.description: the provider's id for it, echoed in the result

source.description: Optional originating request or other source entity.

output.description: what produced the prose beside it: the ask, for a model’s own words, the call whose failure this reports, or the stream it came off (@yaks/process). Worn only by an output; prose a person or a system wrote has none

source.description: the entry or run that produced it

error.description: an outcome the code expected and recorded: normal

exception.description: an outcome the code did not expect, whoever caused it: a defect report, not a stop. Bare, its prose rides the `content` beside it; a host that catches the fault itself fills these, which are its to write and nobody else's

stack.description: where it came from, as the runtime reported it

request.description: what was being served when it threw

execution.description: How a recorded call is going. `running` is the runner’s claim on it — a second host, or a re-entry, leaves it alone; a row still `running` when a process starts is a run that was interrupted, and the boot pass re-drives it.

tool.description: A registered tool that callers can invoke.

call_ready.description: a call nobody has answered and nobody scheduled: run the tool it names and attach the result

call_woken.description: a scheduled call whose wake has fired and nobody has answered: run it now. Inert in a graph that knows no wakes, where the pair is one rule and every call is due when it is written
